notes: Named threats to the Welsh environment. Each belongs to one family on the hazard-families axis of config/taxonomy.json. Gwylio watches hazards, not adversaries.

hazards.name: Ash dieback
hazards.note: Fungal disease (Hymenoscyphus fraxineus) killing ash trees across Wales, with roadside safety and woodland costs.

hazards.name: Phytophthora ramorum
hazards.note: Pathogen of larch and other trees that has driven large-scale felling in Welsh forests.

hazards.name: Avian influenza in wild birds
hazards.note: Highly pathogenic avian influenza in seabirds and other wild birds, and the restrictions that follow.

hazards.name: Invasive non-native plants
hazards.note: Species such as Japanese knotweed and Himalayan balsam spreading along rivers and roads.

hazards.name: Invasive aquatic species
hazards.note: Freshwater and marine invaders such as signal crayfish and killer shrimp.

hazards.name: Drought and low river flows
hazards.note: Dry spells that lower river flows and reservoirs and trigger drought declarations.

hazards.name: River and surface water flooding
hazards.note: Flooding from rivers and intense rainfall, including the communities and infrastructure at risk.

hazards.name: Coastal flooding and erosion
hazards.note: Storm surge, sea level rise and erosion along the Welsh coast.

hazards.name: Coal tip instability
hazards.note: Disused coal tips made unstable by heavy rainfall, a legacy risk concentrated in the South Wales valleys.

hazards.name: Upland and heathland wildfire
hazards.note: Vegetation fires on moorland, heath and forest, often in dry springs.

hazards.name: Agricultural pollution
hazards.note: Nutrient and slurry pollution from farming, including phosphorus in protected rivers.

hazards.name: Storm overflow discharges
hazards.note: Sewage released from storm overflows into rivers and coastal waters.

hazards.name: Metal mine pollution
hazards.note: Metals leaching from abandoned mines into Welsh rivers.

hazards.name: Marine heatwave
hazards.note: Periods of unusually warm sea temperatures that stress marine ecosystems.

hazards.name: Public funding pressure
hazards.note: Real-terms cuts or uncertainty in budgets for environmental bodies and their partners.

hazards.name: Legal challenge
hazards.note: Judicial reviews, complaints and court rulings that test regulators and environmental policy.

hazards.name: Farm support transition
hazards.note: The move from the old farm payments to the Sustainable Farming Scheme and its effect on land use.
